item.caption:
🗳️ Georgia voters have more than candidates to consider on Election Day!

Three proposed constitutional amendments will appear on the Nov. 3 ballot, and each could change how the state handles property taxes, judicial elections or emergency services.

Here's what voters will decide:

🌾 **Amendment 1 — Farmland property taxes:** Would increase the maximum acreage eligible for a special property tax assessment from 2,000 to 4,000 acres.

⚖️ **Amendment 2 — Probate judge elections:** Would require all Georgia probate judges to run in nonpartisan elections, removing political party labels from ballots.

🚨 **Amendment 3 — Emergency 911 funding:** Would allow lawmakers to establish a dedicated fund for maintaining, operating and improving emergency 911 systems without directly creating a new tax or fee.

Each amendment requires a majority of votes cast on that question to pass, and voters can decide on each proposal separately.

Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3.

Read the full breakdown of what a yes or no vote means at The Augusta Press.

Negative partisanship — voting against candidates rather than for them — dominated the campaign's closing days. Polls close in stages Tuesday night across time zones.

item.caption:
we (early) voted! did you?

just a couple more days to do the darn thing, folks! GO #VOTE! we choose #earlyvoting because one #electionday we got caughtttt in line. never again. 

yesterday, around 11AM, we arrived at @stsophiaalb. naturally, we had to get a picture of @mydarlnclementine by the voting sign.

as we’re posing, a group of elderly folks approach the entrance. one gentleman with a walker calls out:
“is she a republican?”
“ew! gosh no! are you?!” 
“of course not,” he says.
“well, good. we’re all playing for the same team then!”
everyone giggled, and his wife piped up, “now don’t go getting us in trouble before we even get in.” 

the whole interaction just warmed the heart. admittedly, first instinct was to make an assumption based on appearances. turns out, assumptions can make an ass out of you. (we’ll own that one.)
a little reminder that people are more than their age, appearance, or the labels we might assign them. also equality, compassion, and looking out for our fellow humans shouldn’t be partisan values - they should just be human values.

now get out there and vote!

Voting is power! If you haven’t voted yet, make a plan to drop off a ballot at an official drop box (it’s too late to mail), or vote in person Tuesday, Nov 3, Election Day. Many states have same day voter registration- check the next slide. If you work on Tuesday, you can still go vote, make a plan with your employer. 
Most info you need to make informed decisions will be coming from state-specific sources, or check any non-profits or publications you admire to see how they suggest voting on different topics. You will feel most confident if you can do research ahead of voting at the polls, or while you are filling out a ballot at home. 
There are also resources to help you check voter registration, find a polling place, see what is on the ballot, and support groups to help get you to the polls or protect your legal right to vote. Try one of these sites or ask a friend! 
www.vote.org 
www.vote411.org 
indivisible.org/campaigns/our-vote
rideshare2vote.com

Tuesday's the day, FXBG. Polls are open 6 a.m. to 7 p.m., an expired Virginia driver's license still counts as ID, and you vote at your assigned polling place, not wherever you voted early. All four school divisions are off Tuesday, so plan around the kids too.

Meanwhile at City Hall, council is working out how close a marijuana store could get to a school. State rules say 1,000 feet, and staff says that would rule out most of downtown. Nothing's decided yet.

Then it's a busy week: six Stafford marching bands for one canned good Monday (it benefits @fredfoodva), a pay-what-you-can Dear Evan Hansen preview at @marywash Wednesday, the @staffordvagov Veterans Day ceremony and First Friday downtown with @visitfxbg on Friday, and Kenmore lit the 1700s way Saturday with @thegeorgewashingtonfoundation.

📸: Fredericksburg City Hall by Antony-22, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

The full Rundown is free at the link in bio.

A little more local. A lot more interesting.

I VOTED – YO VOTÉ! 🇺🇸

I voted a week ago, and I’ve been keeping this little moment to myself, feeling happy and excited about my decision. But today, I want to share with everyone that I did my part and voted!

Every time I hold my ballot in my hands, I feel happy and confident about my decision. I pray for the people and for our country. At that moment, I don’t care who someone is or which political party they belong to. We are all people, and we all deserve a better future.

My hope is that whoever wins the election will always remember the people they represent. Every decision they make and every bill they sign should be for the good of the people and the future of this country.

May our leaders always put America first and never forget the voices of the people.

God bless you, God bless our people, and God bless America! 🇺🇸
